e.) LEO is a bad since you will have roughly 2/3 of the day sun and 1/3 night, therefor still the need for high end Batteries. GEO stationary doesn't have this problem but is 3x more expensive to deliver.

comments.author: @desmond-hawkins
comments.text: (16:52) About computer hardware: "it's easier to cool them in space". Lol no, not by a long shot. In space you have very limited amounts of material into which to transfer heat. Yes you can use cooling loops, and then what do you do with the hot water? There's no air, no extra water. The only way to get rid of heat is by radiating it as infrared, and this is much less efficient than heat conduction into another medium. It's a major challenge for any system outside the atmosphere, and there's not much we can ever do about it: at a fundamental level, we are stuck with radiation and can only use conduction to have the heat be radiated from some other part of the same spacecraft.

comments.author: @kajsing
comments.text:
I have to correct you on the heat issue. In space, heat has to be radiated away, which is extremely slow and requires a much larger surface area.

Also, the amount of waste heat our entire civilization produces is almost comically tiny compared to what Earth receives from the Sun, 
we’re talking many orders of magnitude difference. We’re basically a rounding error in the planet's energy budget.
